Isha Raman: quick design question for the settings bulk-update flow We have multi-section form with many optional fields. Should validation surface inline only, or should we show a compact error summary after submit? Also thinking about whether required-field markers should be visible on collapsed groups. Tom Becker: I prefer inline + a small ephemeral summary that appears after a failed save. The summary should show: count of errors and clickable items to navigate. Keep initial view minimal. Priya Nair: if sections collapse, inline alone will hide errors. Summary is helpful. Make sure summary is keyboard operable (buttons) and announces to screen readers. Ethan Cole: accessibility note: summary should use aria-live="polite" or assertive? If it appears on submit, assertive is ok but we need to avoid double announcements. Maybe use assertive only for first time. Rina Sato: required marker: don't rely solely on color or asterisk. Use text like "(required)" in assistive text for forms where users may not expect requiredness. For collapsed groups, show a condensed badge "2 required" on the collapsed header. Isha Raman: proposal draft: - show inline validation messages under fields (one-line) - on submit failure: show a dismissible summary banner with brief heading "2 problems found" and list of clickable field labels - each list button focuses the field and expands the section if collapsed - when navigating from summary, set aria-describedby on the field to connect to the error message Tom Becker: prototype note: ensure focus management restores to the point where user was before interacting with summary. Don't trap focus. Priya Nair: for the summary we should include an sr-only heading like "Form errors" and a summary sentence for screen readers. Example copy: "There are 3 errors. Press enter on an item to move to the field." Ethan Cole: example markup idea: ```html

Form errors

2 problems found. Use the list to jump to each error.

Environment name is required
``` Rina Sato: small a11y additions: ensure the error message id is referenced in aria-describedby and that when focus moves to the field we call element.scrollIntoView({block: 'center'}) to avoid off-screen positioning for keyboard-only users. Also mobile screen readers behave differently; test on TalkBack/VoiceOver. Isha Raman: destructive confirmation copy question: bulk-archive vs bulk-delete. For permanent delete: typed confirmation preferred. For archive or soft-delete use a simple modal with checkbox. Thoughts on consistency? Tom Becker: agree. Standardize rule: permanent irreversible = typed string, reversible or bulk soft actions = checkbox + primary confirm. Keep copy consistent: "Type DELETE to permanently remove X items." or "Check to confirm archiving X items." Priya Nair: for typed confirmation UX: input should have clear label and instructions, show exact string to type. Provide Cancel and Close with keyboard shortcuts listed. Don't prefill hidden values. accessibility-bot: accessibility-scan: Warning: form-summary lacks role="status" for non-blocking announcements; modal focus trap not configured on branch feature/bulk-form. CI: https://ci.redwood.dev/5678 Isha Raman: action items: - Tom to build an interactive prototype with focus-jump and restore; include collapsed-section behavior. Due Tue. - Priya to author microcopy guidelines for required markers and confirmation dialogs. Due Thu. - Rina to create a testing matrix for screen readers + mobile. Due Fri. Tom Becker: ok starting prototype now. I'll post Figma + Codesandbox link when ready. Priya Nair: I'll draft the copy and post examples for typed vs checkbox confirmations. Rina Sato: will start accessibility tests after prototype link. Isha Raman: thanks all will follow up in a week.
